2609.29056.title: Empath: Tracing Multi-Level Emotion Dynamics in Crisis Counseling Dialogues
2609.29056.paper_summary: Emotion dynamics are critical for understanding crisis-support conversations, yet most computational work treats emotion as static utterance-level labels. We introduce EMPATH, a framework for understanding affective dynamics in mental health dialogues across three granularities: turn-level labels, transition probabilities, and global conversation archetypes. Applying EMPATH to text-based crisis conversations with self-identified Black texters discussing grief, we find persistent negative affect, gradual hope-ward transitions, distinct texter-volunteer emotional roles, and heterogeneous recovery trajectories. These results highlight the informative patterns that emerge from computationally understanding crisis support and expressions of grief as dynamic processes within conversations, as well as the overall value of emotion-dynamic analysis for analyzing and comparing affect in dialogues.
2609.29056.paper_summary_zh: 情感動態對於理解危機支持對話至關重要，然而大多數計算工作將情感視為靜態的發話級別標籤。<lb/>我們介紹EMPATH，一個用於理解心理健康對話中情感動態的框架，涵蓋三個層面：發話級別標籤、轉換概率和全局對話原型。<lb/>將EMPATH應用於自我認同為黑人發信者的文本危機對話，討論悲傷時，我們發現持續的負面情感、逐漸向希望轉變、發信者與志願者之間明顯的情感角色，以及異質的恢復軌跡。<lb/>這些結果突顯了從計算理解危機支持和悲傷表達中出現的信息模式，將其視為對話中的動態過程，以及情感動態分析在分析和比較對話中的情感方面的整體價值。
